scripts.purpose: Shared helpers: CameraConfig and frame-recarray construction (same as create_initial_frame_rec_array), synthetic frames, stats, environment and load capture

(a) Real CameraGroupSharedMemory.create(read_only=True) in the parent and 1-5 spawned writers calling CameraSharedMemoryRingBuffer.put_frame(overwrite=True), unthrottled for 10 s after a first lap, both sizes, plus a single np.copyto reference

(b) Reader styles get_latest_data (reused or allocating), get_data_by_index, get_next_data, get_latest_multiframe, get_images_by_frame_number and view references, cold and warm, against 5 spawned 60 fps writers, 5 interleaved rounds
(c) Real VideoRecorder.create and record_frame in 5 (or 1) spawned processes, paced at 60 fps for 20 s and unthrottled for 10 s, with CPU%, release time and frames counted in the output files
(d) Real UI serialisation: get_latest_multiframe or get_images_by_frame_number followed by create_frontend_payload for 5 cameras, in a relay-style await_10ms loop or a no-sleep loop

(e) Real WorkerRegistry(PROCESS), CameraGroupManager, CameraGroup and camera processes running run_opencv_camera_loop with lockstep, put_frame, VideoRecorder, start/stop_recording and RecordingFinalizer, plus a UI consumer. create_cv2_video_capture is monkeypatched in-process to a FakeCapture with a 60 fps free-running sensor (latest frame wins); retrieve is either mjpeg (imdecode) or memcpy

limitations: Idle is defined by background CPU (processes outside the benchmark tree) mean and p95 < 10% and system CPU < 10% before and after. The alternative measure system-minus-tree reached a 9.1-10.3% mean in the heaviest runs (c_record, 1080p mjpeg e2e). That is attributed to kernel work caused by the benchmark itself (`System` up to 7.7% while files were written) and to sampling misalignment. This is an inference.
Each configuration was run as before: 1 run for most configurations, 2 for 1080p mjpeg+UI, 1080p memcpy+UI and 720p memcpy+UI. The UI-off effect rests on 1 run.

No real cameras were used. The e2e capture is FakeCapture with assumed buffer-size-1 'latest frame wins' semantics. Whether DSHOW decodes MJPEG inside retrieve() (mjpeg mode) or elsewhere (closer to memcpy mode) is still open. The mjpeg stand-in adds one memcpy, and its q90 synthetic JPEGs may differ from a real camera's.

Encode cost and file sizes depend on the synthetic content. Whether MSMF H.264 runs on the GPU or in software was not established. Why the paced runs used more encoder CPU when idle (476% vs 380% at 720p) was not investigated.
Unthrottled encode throughputs are derived (frames / (elapsed + release)), because MSMF write() is asynchronous.

Copy counting (bench_f) is single-process with in-process wrappers. The JPEG tobytes, assemble and slice copies are analytic. Copies inside DSHOW, MSMF, the encoder and the websocket stack cannot be counted.
The UI benchmarks have no browser (instant ack, no websocket send), so UI rates are server-side upper bounds.
Power plan was Balanced and CPU frequency was not pinned; turbo and thermal state can still move absolute numbers between runs.

bench_common.SCRATCH_TMP is hard-coded to the 2026-10-25 session's scratch folder (bench_common.py L23-27). It worked unchanged. bench_f left 20.8 MB there, which was deleted after logging (results\bench_tmp_leftover_sizes_before_delete.txt). Empty c_rec_* folders remain.
